passage_claims.claim: Parliament cleared the Amendment Bill 2026; LS passed 24 Mar 2026 by voice vote amid Opposition walkout
Introduced in Lok Sabha mid-March 2026 (13 March) by Social Justice Minister Virendra Kumar
passage_claims.note: Wikipedia infobox/text inconsistent on date, but news outlets agree on 13 March.

passage_claims.claim: Rajya Sabha passed it 25 March 2026 by voice vote after rejecting a motion to refer to a select committee
passage_claims.note: 25 March passage confirmed by many; the select-committee rejection was found reported for the Lok Sabha, not clearly for the Rajya Sabha. Voice vote in RS not independently checked.
Gazette notification reported 30 March; Wikipedia agrees.

passage_claims.claim: Minister said bill protects people facing discrimination due to biological factors
passage_claims.note: Reported as 'severe social exclusion due to biological condition'.

passage_claims.claim: Minister told the House district magistrates would issue identity certificates and a medical board would assist
passage_claims.note: Search found the medical board mechanism (certification by board headed by CMO/Dy CMO) but no DM role in the 2026 amendment or minister's reply. Reports say the minister's reply was ~2 minutes and gave no clarifications. Likely wrong or misattributed.

passage_claims.claim: Graded punishments, heavier for forced transgender identity / begging / servitude, higher where victim is a child
passage_claims.note: Enhanced penalties for forced identity and exploitation confirmed generally; child-victim detail not independently checked.

passage_claims.claim: Amended law narrows definition (intersex, kinner, hijra, aravani, jogta) and makes medical certification required; removes self-perceived identity
passage_claims.note: Specific list of identities not individually verified.

passage_claims.claim: NALSA judgment (SC) recognised third gender and self-identification without surgery
Under the 2019 Act a person applied to the DM for a certificate that conferred the right to self-perceived identity
passage_claims.note: 2019 Act s.4 gives the right to self-perceived identity and ss.5-6 the DM certificate; the phrasing that the certificate 'conferred' the right is loose.

passage_claims.claim: Opposition (incl. Congress) called it unconstitutional regression; alleged exclusion of gay/lesbian persons
passage_claims.note: 'Regression' confirmed; Congress attribution and gay/lesbian allegation not individually checked.

questions.note: NALSA 15 April 2014; year not in passage; distractors wrong. Cited source is Wikipedia page of the 2019 Act, acceptable but a NALSA source would be better.
Art 110 Money Bills, 112 budget, 113 estimates procedure. Unambiguous, though Art 111 appears in several questions (redundant with Q3, Q4, Q6).

questions.my_answer: Both true; R explains A or not is arguable
questions.note: A is true and R is true, but the Act becoming law on assent is exactly what Art 111 provides, so 0 (R explains A) is defensible as well as 1. Two defensible answers. No clean repair at same index; recommend DROP (or replace with a clearer A/R pair).
Art 21 life/liberty, Art 32 constitutional remedies, Art 111 assent, Art 368 amendment procedure. Distractor mappings all wrong. Standard textbook facts.
In force 10 Jan 2020 by S.O. 135(E); passed Nov 2019, assent 5 Dec 2019 (indiacode).

Art 368(2): majority of total membership + two-thirds present and voting, President shall give assent (24th Amdt). Art 111 proviso allows return of non-Money Bill. Art 32 is SC; HCs use Art 226 (and SC is not the only forum, 'only High Courts' is false). Minor: source cites only Art 368 while Art 111 and 32 claims need other sources.

passage_fixes.old: He told the House that district magistrates would issue identity certificates to transgender persons, and that a medical board would assist in the identification process.
passage_fixes.new: The amended law routes recognition through certification by a medical board.
passage_fixes.reason: DM role in the minister's reply is unverifiable; reports describe a medical-board mechanism only.

passage_fixes.old: On 25 March 2026, the Upper House passed it by voice vote after rejecting a motion to refer the Bill to a select parliamentary committee.
passage_fixes.new: On 25 March 2026, the Upper House passed it.
passage_fixes.reason: Select-committee rejection reported for the Lok Sabha; RS voice vote and rejection not independently confirmed.

summary: Core timeline (introduced 13 Mar, LS 24 Mar, RS 25 Mar, assent 30 Mar 2026) is confirmed by multiple publishers. Two passage details (DM issuing certificates per minister; RS select-committee motion) are unverified and should be trimmed. Questions 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 are sound; Q3 assertion-reason is ambiguous between answers 0 and 1 and should be dropped.
